label.en: official of the Directorate of Astronomy
official of the Directorate of Astronomy

place.en: from Bianjing to the Central Capital

sourceDate.text: 陳氏因梁，亦用祖沖之歷

translationRepairs: To find the next month: long month add 2 days; short month add 1 day; day remainder always 20,779.
Chinese 求次月：大月加二日，小月加一日，日餘皆二萬七百七十九 is truncated in the current idiomatic; the long/short-month rule and day remainder 20,779 belong on this unit, not the next.
To seek the next month: long month add 2 days; short month add 1 day; day remainder in each case 20,779.
Literal is likewise truncated; 大月加二日，小月加一日，日餘皆二萬七百七十九 must be rendered on s0121.
Long month: add 2 days; short month: add 1 day; day remainder always 20,779.
When the sequence reaches 13 days with day remainder 15,987.5, drop that cycle.
Chinese 歷滿十三日，日餘萬五千九百八十七半，則去之 does not mention long/short months; that English belongs to s0121, and this unit needs the 13-day / 15,987.5 drop rule.
Long month: add 2 days; short month: add 1 day; day remainder in each case 20,779.
When the sequence fills 13 days and day remainder 15,987.5, then remove it.
Literal mismatch: s0122 Chinese is the fill-13-days removal rule, not the long/short-month increments.
When the sequence reaches 13 days with day remainder 15,987.5, drop that cycle.
At yang's end one enters yin; at yin's end one enters yang.
Chinese 陽竟入陰，陰竟入陽 is the yang/yin switch, not the 13-day remainder rule currently shown.
When the sequence fills 13 days and day remainder 15,987.5, then remove it.
When yang ends, enter yin; when yin ends, enter yang.
Literal must follow 陽竟入陰，陰竟入陽 rather than the preceding cycle-drop sentence.
At yang's end one enters yin; at yin's end one enters yang.
For the next day: add one day.
Chinese 求次日：加一日 is simply add one day for the next day; the yang/yin-end wording belongs on s0123.
When yang ends, enter yin; when yin ends, enter yang.
To seek the next day: add one day.
Literal for 求次日：加一日 is 'add one day', not the yang/yin transition.
For the next day: add one day.
For new/full moon correction: multiply new-moon fractional remainder by 2,029; divide by 303 for day remainder; double the remainder for small parts to get new-moon difference.
Chinese 求朔望差 with multipliers 二千二十九 and 三百三 is the new/full-moon difference procedure, wrongly labeled as 'next day'.
To seek the next day: add one day.

To seek new- and full-moon difference: multiply new-moon small remainder by 2,029; when full of 303 it makes day remainder; what does not fill, double it for small parts: that is new-moon difference number.
Literal must restore the 朔望差 algorithm (×2,029 / 303, double remainder for small parts).
For new/full moon correction: multiply new-moon fractional remainder by 2,029; divide by 303 for day remainder; double the remainder for small parts to get new-moon difference.
Add 14 days, day remainder 20,186, and small parts 125.
Chinese 加一十四日，日餘二萬一百八十六，小分百二十五 is the add-14-days step with day remainder 20,186 (not the prior 朔望差 procedure, and not 21,186).

To seek new- and full-moon difference: multiply new-moon small remainder by 2,029; when full of 303 it makes day remainder; what does not fill, double it for small parts: that is new-moon difference number.
Add 14 days; day remainder 20,186; small parts 125.
Literal correctly realigns to 十四日 / 二萬一百八十六 / 百二十五.
Add 14 days, day remainder 21,186, and small parts 125.
When small parts reach 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, convert to days for full-moon difference.
Chinese 小分滿六百六從日餘…即望差數也 is the small-parts carry to full-moon difference, not the 14-day add.
Add 14 days; day remainder 21,186; small parts 125.
When small parts fill 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, it makes days: that is full-moon difference number.
Literal must follow the 六百六 carry / 望差數 wording of s0127.
When small parts reach 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, convert to days for full-moon difference.
Add again for the following new moon.
Chinese 又加之，後月朔也 is 'add again for the following new moon', not the small-parts carry rule.
When small parts fill 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, it makes days: that is full-moon difference number.
Add again for the next month's new moon.
Literal for 又加之，後月朔也 is the next-month new-moon add, not 望差 carry.
Add again for the following new moon.
For conjunction and eclipse: take midnight yin-yang sequence entry and remainder at new/full moon, drop halves, set small parts 303, and add the difference number.
Chinese 求合朔月食 with 有半者去之 and 小分三百三 is the conjunction/eclipse setup, not 'add again'.
Add again for the next month's new moon.
To seek conjunction and lunar eclipse: set new- and full-moon midnight yin-yang sequence entry and remainder; when there is a half, remove it; set small parts 303; add the difference number.
Literal must restore the 合朔月食 procedure of this unit.
For conjunction and eclipse: take midnight yin-yang sequence entry and remainder at new/full moon, drop halves, set small parts 303, and add the difference number.
Carry small parts into day remainder and day remainder into days; when days complete one sequence, subtract the cycle.
Chinese 小分滿六百六從日餘，日餘滿通法從日，日滿一歷去之 is the carry/remove-cycle rule, not conjunction setup.
To seek conjunction and lunar eclipse: set new- and full-moon midnight yin-yang sequence entry and remainder; when there is a half, remove it; set small parts 303; add the difference number.
When small parts fill 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, carry to days; when days fill one sequence, remove it.
Literal correctly realigns to the 從日 / 一歷去之 carry chain.
Carry small parts into day remainder and day remainder into days; when days complete one sequence, subtract the cycle.
Name the day (outside the count) for sequence entry at the instant of new or full moon.
Chinese 命日算外，則朔望加時入歷也 names the day for hour-entry, not the prior carry rule.
When small parts fill 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, carry to days; when days fill one sequence, remove it.
Name the day, outside the count: then the sequence entry at the hour of new or full moon.
Literal must follow 命日算外…朔望加時入歷.
Name the day (outside the count) for sequence entry at the instant of new or full moon.
If hour-entry is 1 day with remainder ≤4,198 and small parts ≤428, or 12 days with remainder ≥11,788 and small parts ≥481, new moon yields conjunction and full moon yields eclipse.
Chinese gives the 一日/12日 remainder thresholds for 交會 and 月食; current English is only the naming formula from s0131.
Name the day, outside the count: then the sequence entry at the hour of new or full moon.

When new- or full-moon hour sequence entry is one day and day remainder 4,198 with small parts 428 or below, or twelve days with day remainder 11,788 and small parts 481 or above, at new moon there is conjunction; at full moon, lunar eclipse.
Literal restores the conjunction/eclipse threshold conditions of s0132.
If hour-entry is 1 day with remainder ≤4,198 and small parts ≤428, or 12 days with remainder ≥11,788 and small parts ≥481, new moon yields conjunction and full moon yields eclipse.
For fixed remainders at conjunction/eclipse: add difference day remainder to midnight slow-fast remainder; carry into days when remainder fills communication factor.
Chinese 求合朔月食定大小餘 adds difference remainder to midnight slow-fast remainder; it is not the threshold sentence.

When new- or full-moon hour sequence entry is one day and day remainder 4,198 with small parts 428 or below, or twelve days with day remainder 11,788 and small parts 481 or above, at new moon there is conjunction; at full moon, lunar eclipse.

To seek the fixed greater and smaller remainders for conjunction and eclipse: let difference-number day remainder add to midnight slow-fast sequence remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, carry to days: then sequence entry at the hour of new or full moon.
Literal must restore the 定大小餘 / 遲疾歷余 procedure.
For fixed remainders at conjunction/eclipse: add difference day remainder to midnight slow-fast remainder; carry into days when remainder fills communication factor.
Multiply sequence remainder by adjustment rate, adjust surplus-deficit parts, scale by difference factor, then subtract surplus or add deficit from base new/full fractional remainder.
Chinese 以入歷余乘損益率…為定小餘 is the rate/surplus-deficit adjustment, not the prior fixed-remainder setup.

To seek the fixed greater and smaller remainders for conjunction and eclipse: let difference-number day remainder add to midnight slow-fast sequence remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, carry to days: then sequence entry at the hour of new or full moon.

Multiply sequence-entry remainder by decrease-increase rate; by decrease-increase adjust accumulated surplus-deficit parts; as difference factor to one; subtract surplus and add deficit from the original new/full small remainder for fixed small remainder.
Literal correctly realigns to the 損益率 / 盈縮積分 / 定小餘 wording.
Multiply sequence remainder by adjustment rate, adjust surplus-deficit parts, scale by difference factor, then subtract surplus or add deficit from base new/full fractional remainder.
On overflow or underflow in adjustment, carry or borrow using the day factor.
Chinese 益之或滿法，損之或不足，以日法進退日 is overflow/underflow by the day factor, not the multiply-by-rate sentence.

Multiply sequence-entry remainder by decrease-increase rate; by decrease-increase adjust accumulated surplus-deficit parts; as difference factor to one; subtract surplus and add deficit from the original new/full small remainder for fixed small remainder.
When increasing fills the factor or decreasing is insufficient, advance or retreat by the day factor.
Literal must follow 以日法進退日.
On overflow or underflow in adjustment, carry or borrow using the day factor.
For event hour: multiply fixed fractional remainder by 12, divide by day factor for double-hours; count from zi (outside the count).
Chinese 求合朔月食加時：以十二乘定小餘…命以子 is the event-hour procedure, not the overflow rule.
When increasing fills the factor or decreasing is insufficient, advance or retreat by the day factor.
To seek the hour of conjunction and eclipse: multiply fixed small remainder by 12; when full of day factor obtain one double-hour; name from zi, outside the count: the double-hour of the event.
Literal restores ×12 / 日法 / 子 naming for the event hour.
For event hour: multiply fixed fractional remainder by 12, divide by day factor for double-hours; count from zi (outside the count).
If remainder remains, multiply by four; each day-factor quotient gives minor (shao), half (ban), or major (tai) subdivisions.
Chinese 有餘者四之…為少、二為半、三為太 is the quadruple-remainder subdivision, not the hour procedure.
To seek the hour of conjunction and eclipse: multiply fixed small remainder by 12; when full of day factor obtain one double-hour; name from zi, outside the count: the double-hour of the event.
When there is remainder, quadruple it; when full of day factor obtain one as minor, two as half, three as major.
Literal must follow 四之…少/半/太.
If remainder remains, multiply by four; each day-factor quotient gives minor (shao), half (ban), or major (tai) subdivisions.
Further remainder: multiply by three; quotients are strong (qiang); combine with prior subdivisions for compound labels.
Chinese 又有餘者三之…為強 and the 少強/半強/太強 compounds belong here, not the quadruple rule.
When there is remainder, quadruple it; when full of day factor obtain one as minor, two as half, three as major.
When there is still remainder, triple it; when full of day factor obtain one as strong; combine strong with minor for minor-strong, with half for half-strong, with major for major-strong.
Literal correctly realigns to 三之…強 and the compound labels.
Further remainder: multiply by three; quotients are strong (qiang); combine with prior subdivisions for compound labels.
Two quotients yield minor-weak; combine upward through half-weak and major-weak to a full weak double-hour named from the prior hour.
Chinese 得二者為少弱…以前辰名之 is the weak-subdivision ladder, not the strong-compound sentence.
When there is still remainder, triple it; when full of day factor obtain one as strong; combine strong with minor for minor-strong, with half for half-strong, with major for major-strong.
When two are obtained, that is minor-weak; combine with minor for half-weak, with half for major-weak, with major for one double-hour weak; name by the preceding double-hour.
Literal must follow 少弱/半弱/太弱/一辰弱 naming.
Two quotients yield minor-weak; combine upward through half-weak and major-weak to a full weak double-hour named from the prior hour.
For lunar latitude: take yin-yang sequence remainder, multiply by adjustment rate, divide by communication factor, and adjust the combined number.
Chinese 求月去日道度 begins lunar latitude from the solar path; current English is still the weak-hour labels.
When two are obtained, that is minor-weak; combine with minor for half-weak, with half for major-weak, with major for one double-hour weak; name by the preceding double-hour.

To seek the moon's degrees from the solar path: set yin-yang sequence remainder, multiply by decrease-increase rate, as communication factor to one, by decrease-increase adjust the combined number for the fixed value.
Literal restores the 月去日道度 / 損益兼數 procedure.
For lunar latitude: take yin-yang sequence remainder, multiply by adjustment rate, divide by communication factor, and adjust the combined number.
Divide the fixed number by twelve for degrees.
Chinese 定數十二而一為度 converts the fixed number to degrees by twelves, not the latitude setup.

To seek the moon's degrees from the solar path: set yin-yang sequence remainder, multiply by decrease-increase rate, as communication factor to one, by decrease-increase adjust the combined number for the fixed value.
Fixed number: twelve to one makes degrees.
Literal must follow 定數十二而一為度.
Divide the fixed number by twelve for degrees.
The remainder in quarters yields minor, half, and major subdivisions.
Chinese 不盡四而一，為少、半、太 is quarter subdivisions of the remainder, not dividing by twelve.
Fixed number: twelve to one makes degrees.
What does not fill: four to one makes minor, half, and major.
Literal correctly realigns to 四而一…少、半、太.
The remainder in quarters yields minor, half, and major subdivisions.
Further remainder in thirds: one gives strong, two minor-weak, completing lunar distance from the ecliptic.
Chinese 又不盡者三而一，一為強，二為少弱 completes lunar distance; it is not the quarter-remainder sentence.
What does not fill: four to one makes minor, half, and major.
When still not filled, three to one: one is strong, two is minor-weak: that is the moon's degrees from the solar path.
Literal must follow 三而一…強/少弱…月去日道數.
Further remainder in thirds: one gives strong, two minor-weak, completing lunar distance from the ecliptic.
Yang sequence is outside the path; yin sequence inside.
Chinese 陽歷在表，陰歷在裏 is outside/inside the path, not the thirds-remainder rule.
When still not filled, three to one: one is strong, two is minor-weak: that is the moon's degrees from the solar path.
Yang sequence is outside; yin sequence is inside.
Literal correctly realigns to 陽歷在表，陰歷在裏.
Yang sequence is outside the path; yin sequence inside.
Measured gnomon shadows, clepsydra marks, and culmination-star numbers:
Chinese 測景漏刻中星數： is the gnomon/clepsydra/culmination-star heading, not the yang/yin path note.
Yang sequence is outside; yin sequence is inside.
Numbers for measuring the gnomon shadow, clepsydra marks, and culmination stars:
Literal restores the measuring-numbers section title of s0145.
Fast: 1 degree 6 parts per day for 23 days.
Prograde, slow: twenty parts per day for 8 days.
Chinese 從，遲，日行二十分，八日 is prograde slow at twenty parts for 8 days; current English is the next unit's fast motion.
Fast, daily one degree six parts; 23 days.
Prograde, slow, daily twenty parts; 8 days.
Literal must follow 從，遲…二十分，八日.
Morning concealment east; day and degree remainders as at first.
Fast: 1 degree 6 parts per day for 23 days.
Chinese 疾，日行一度六分，二十三日 is fast 1 degree 6 parts for 23 days, not morning concealment.
Morning concealment in the east; day and degree remainder as at first.
Fast, daily one degree six parts; 23 days.
Literal correctly realigns to 疾…一度六分，二十三日.
Morning concealment east; day and degree remainders as at first.
Chinese 晨伏東方，日度餘如初 is morning concealment in the east, not the 115-day cycle summary.
One cycle 115 days, day remainder 34,739; planetary motion the same.
Morning concealment in the east; day and degree remainder as at first.
Literal must follow 晨伏東方，日度餘如初.
Chinese 一終百一十五日，日餘三萬四千七百三十九 is one cycle of 115 days (remainder 34,739), not the conjunction figure.
One conjunction 57 days, day remainder 37,115; planetary motion likewise.
One cycle 115 days, day remainder 34,739; planetary motion the same.
Literal correctly realigns to 一終百一十五日…三萬四千七百三十九.
At upper-origin year jiazi: civil new year jiazi new moon, winter solstice at midnight; sun, moon, and five planets at the start of Void; yin-yang and slow-fast sequences also begin here.
Chinese 一合五十七日，日餘三萬七千一百一十五 is one conjunction of 57 days (remainder 37,115); the upper-origin epoch text belongs on s0219.

In a year of the upper origin, the year is in jiazi; civil new year, jiazi new moon, midnight winter solstice; sun, moon, and five planets gather at the beginning of the lodge Void; yin-yang, slow-fast likewise begin from this.
One conjunction 57 days, day remainder 37,115; planetary motion likewise.
Literal must follow 一合五十七日…三萬七千一百一十五, not the upper-origin gathering.
In Song Daming year 6 (462 CE) Zu Chongzhi presented the Jiazi Epoch Calendar methods; before adoption they were called the Great Brightness Calendar.
In the sixth year of Emperor Wu of Song's Daming reign (462 CE), Zu Chongzhi presented the Jiazi Epoch Calendar methods; before adoption they were called the Great Brightness Calendar.
Chinese 宋武帝大明六年 names Emperor Wu of Song; the idiomatic 'Song Daming year 6' drops 宋武帝 while keeping the rest accurately.
Liang Tianjian year 3: Zu Chongzhi's son Heng memorialized that He Chengtian's calendar was erroneous and unusable.
In Tianjian 3 (504), during the reign of Emperor Wu of Liang, Zu Chongzhi's son Heng memorialized that He Chengtian's calendar was erroneous and unusable.
Chinese 梁武帝天監三年 names Emperor Wu of Liang. The revision restores his standard English name and the date while avoiding the awkward possessive phrase 'Liang Emperor Wu's Tianjian reign.'
